title: BIS Quarterly Review, December 2025
summary: The BIS Quarterly Review December 2025 provides comprehensive coverage of international banking and financial market developments, with primary focus on FX and interest rate derivatives market structure following the 2025 Triennial Survey. Key themes include the surge in FX trading volumes in April 2025 driven by hedging activity, the structural shift in interest rate derivatives markets following the Libor transition, and the growth of the cash-futures basis trade as a dominant market structure feature.
key_points: FX volumes surged significantly in April 2025, with hedging activity and tariff-related news cited as primary drivers of the increase in trading activity
The cash-futures basis trade has emerged as a central mechanism in interest rate derivatives markets, with turnover growth linked to shifts in monetary policy expectations
The transition from Libor to alternative reference rates has structurally reshaped OTC interest rate derivatives markets, with euro contracts migrating to Germany
Global FX markets show uneven progress in emerging market currency trading, with renminbi cited as a key driver of EME currency trading growth
Hedge funds have increased their relative value trades in US Treasuries and interest rate swaps, contributing to basis trade activity
Clearing concentration in OTC interest rate derivatives markets presents challenges for emerging market economies
Risk assets held ground despite growing volatility concerns, while sovereign yields moderated with monetary easing expectations
why_it_matters: This BIS Quarterly Review provides critical market structure intelligence on the plumbing of global FX and rates markets. The 2025 Triennial Survey data embedded in this publication represents the most authoritative snapshot of global foreign exchange market activity, informing how market participants understand liquidity, hedging flows, and structural shifts in trading mechanisms. The focus on basis trade dynamics and Libor transition effects is particularly relevant for fixed income desks and macro strategies.
macro_context: While primarily focused on market structure, the review notes that sovereign yields moderated amid monetary easing expectations, risk assets held ground despite volatility concerns, and the USD and precious metals appreciated. The macro context is secondary to the market structure focus.
market_structure_context: This is the primary focus of the source. Key market structure topics covered: FX market trading mechanisms and liquidity conditions; cash-futures basis trade dynamics; Libor transition and interest rate derivatives market restructuring; broker-dealer and clearing infrastructure; concentration of clearing in OTC derivatives; EME FX and derivatives market development; non-visible trading and its effect on FX liquidity; FX trade execution landscape evolution.
